1.title: A Servant of God
1.context: Paul opens his shortest pastoral with a title he uses in no other greeting: servant of God and apostle of Jesus Christ. The commission's purpose is stated at once, the faith of God's elect and knowledge of the truth that leads to godliness.
1.question: What would it change in your work if its stated purpose were the faith and godliness of the people it reaches?

1.title: Promised Before Time Began
1.context: Eternal life rests on a promise made before time began by the God who cannot lie, and made evident in his own time through the proclamation entrusted to Paul.
1.question: Where do you need to trust a promise whose timing is not yours?

1.title: My True Child in Our Common Faith
1.context: Titus is greeted as Paul's true child in the faith they share. This greeting carries grace and peace only, where the Timothy greetings add mercy; the letter states the difference and builds nothing on it. The framing look ahead to the working letter rides this scene.
1.question: Who has been a true child, or a true parent, to you in the faith?

2.title: Set in Order What Was Unfinished
2.context: Paul left Crete with churches gathered in town after town and the work unfinished: no appointed elders. Titus is sent to finish it, appointing locally in every town. Blameless means a life against which no charge sticks. The reflection on the island's state rides this scene.
2.question: What unfinished work have you been left holding, and what is its next faithful step?

2.title: Blameless, Beginning at Home
2.context: The elder's household is the first evidence: husband of one wife, children who are believers and not open to accusation of indiscretion or insubordination.
2.question: What does your own household say about your readiness to be trusted with more?

2.title: God's Steward
2.context: An overseer is God's steward, answerable for a household that is not his. The negative list and the positive list together describe a man safe to follow. The reflection on the steward's weight, and this list beside 1 Timothy's, rides this scene.
2.question: What has been entrusted to you as a steward rather than an owner?

2.title: Hold Firmly to the Faithful Word
2.context: The elder must hold the word as it was taught so he can encourage by sound teaching and refute those who contradict it. Crete's problem was talkers; this is the qualification that answers them.
2.question: Where do you need to hold more firmly before you can help anyone else hold on?

3.title: They Must Be Silenced
3.context: Rebellious empty talkers, especially those of the circumcision, undermine entire households for dishonorable gain. Households were the units of the ancient world, so an error that captured one captured a small community.
3.question: Where have you seen teaching shaped to please hearers do quiet damage?

3.title: A Cretan Against the Cretans
3.context: Paul quotes one of Crete's own prophets, traditionally named as Epimenides, and endorses the verdict so the rebuke will make them sound in the faith. The reflections on the talkers' identity and their household damage ride this scene.
3.question: What hard truth about your own people have you needed to hear from inside?

3.title: They Profess to Know God
3.context: To the pure all things are pure; to the defiled, nothing is. The talkers profess to know God and deny him by their actions, the measure this letter applies to every profession.
3.question: Where might your actions be telling a different story than your profession?

4.title: Older Men and Older Women
4.context: Sound doctrine is taught by household. Older men are to be temperate, dignified, self-controlled, and sound in faith, love, and perseverance; older women reverent, not slanderers, teachers of good.
4.question: What has an older believer's steadiness taught you that a book could not?

4.title: Train the Young Women
4.context: The older women train the younger to love their husbands and children and manage their households, so that the word of God will not be discredited. Affection here is treated as something that can be trained.
4.question: What have you treated as a feeling that this passage treats as a practice?

4.title: Show Yourself an Example
4.context: The younger men are urged to self-control, and Titus himself is the method: an example in good works, with integrity, dignity, and wholesome speech, so opponents have nothing bad to say. The reflection on teaching traveling hand to hand rides this scene.
4.question: Where does your example currently say more than your words, for better or worse?

4.title: Adorn the Teaching
4.context: Slaves, the least standing of anyone addressed, are told their honest faithfulness will adorn the teaching about God our Savior. The reflection on conduct as doctrine's decoration rides this scene.
4.question: What part of your ordinary work could adorn the teaching this week?

5.title: Grace the Teacher
5.context: The grace of God has appeared, bringing salvation to everyone, and grace instructs: renounce ungodliness and live godly lives in the present age, the age between an appearing that happened and one that has not.
5.question: What is grace currently instructing you to renounce, and to practice?

5.title: The Blessed Hope
5.context: The godly life is lived awaiting the blessed hope and glorious appearance of our great God and Savior Jesus Christ, in the letter's exact words. The reflection on grace's wide scope rides this scene.
5.question: How does waiting for that appearance change an ordinary day?

5.title: Zealous for Good Deeds
5.context: He gave himself to redeem from all lawlessness and purify a people of his own, zealous for good deeds. The reflection on the letter's appearing thread rides this scene.
5.question: What good deed would your zeal choose if it were aimed the way this verse aims it?

5.title: Let No One Despise You
5.context: Speak, encourage, and rebuke with all authority. The young delegate is not to apologize for the message grace has given him to carry.
5.question: Where do you need to stop apologizing for a responsibility you were actually given?

6.title: Peaceable and Gentle to Everyone
6.context: Submit to rulers, be ready for every good work, malign no one. The order is given without qualifications in a province governed by Rome, and it completes the household picture by opening the front door. The reflection on the outward posture rides this scene.
6.question: What would readiness for every good work look like in your street this week?

6.title: We Too Were Foolish
6.context: Gentleness toward outsiders is built on honesty about the past: we too were foolish, disobedient, misled, enslaved, living in malice and envy. Paul includes himself in the list.
6.question: How does remembering your own past change how you treat people still in it?

6.title: Not by the Righteous Deeds We Had Done
6.context: When the kindness of God our Savior appeared, he saved us by mercy, through the washing of new birth and renewal by the Holy Spirit, making us heirs with the hope of eternal life. The reflection on the letter's frame and the washing rides this scene.
6.question: Where are you still trying to be saved by your deeds instead of receiving mercy?

6.title: This Saying Is Trustworthy
6.context: Paul seals the passage as trustworthy and aims it at practice: those who have believed God are to devote themselves to good deeds, excellent and profitable for the people.
6.question: What excellent and profitable deed is this trustworthy saying asking of you?

7.title: Reject a Divisive Man
7.context: Foolish controversies are pointless and worthless. A divisive man is admonished once, then again, and only then rejected, self-condemned by his refusals. The reflection on the procedure's patience rides this scene.
7.question: Where do you need the patience of two honest warnings before a firm boundary?

7.title: Come to Me at Nicopolis
7.context: Artemas or Tychicus will relieve Titus, who is to come to Paul at Nicopolis for the winter. Zenas the lawyer and Apollos are to be equipped for their journey. The reflection on the travelers rides this scene.
7.question: Who could you equip for their journey this week, practically and on purpose?

7.title: Meet the Pressing Needs of Others
7.context: The letter's drumbeat, widened to everyone: learn to devote yourselves to good works in order to meet pressing needs, so as not to be unfruitful.
7.question: Whose pressing need is nearest to you right now, and what is your first step toward it?

7.title: Grace Be with All of You
7.context: Greetings from all who are with Paul, to those who love us in the faith, and the final word over a hard assignment is grace, to all of them, plural.
7.question: Who needs to hear a word of grace from you before this week ends?
